entities.summary:
The ORCID iD, established circa 2012, is a nonproprietary alphanumeric code designed to uniquely identify academic authors and researchers globally. It emerged from a collaborative effort led by the ORCID organization, a nonprofit founded by an international consortium of universities, publishers, and funding agencies. This initiative was driven by the need for a robust solution to the increasingly complex issue of author identification in scholarly communication, which had become muddled by name duplications and variations in author names across different publications.

The ORCID iD allows researchers to maintain a persistent digital identity, linking their work across various platforms, and thus facilitates better attribution of academic contributions. Over the years, ORCID has expanded its reach, with millions of researchers now registered and over 1,200 organizations integrating ORCID iDs into their systems. This integration aids in streamlining grant applications, publication processes, and research assessments, ensuring that authors receive proper credit for their work.

The introduction of the ORCID iD has transformed the landscape of academic publishing and research funding by promoting transparency and accountability. Its standardized approach has been adopted widely, with an increasing number of institutions and publishers mandating ORCID iDs for authors. This shift has led to a more organized and efficient system for tracking academic contributions, ultimately impacting scholarly communication and collaboration across disciplines.

As of 2023, ORCID iDs are linked to over 30 million works, showcasing the vast influence of this system. It has been said, 'The ORCID iD is the backbone of the modern research ecosystem,' emphasizing its critical role in facilitating connections between researchers, their work, and the broader academic community.
